title: What one row lets presolve conclude

blocks.text: A pole-inspection model has many rows of the form
\sum_{j} a_j\, x_j \le b, \qquad x_j \in \{0, 1\}, \quad lo_j \le x_j \le hi_j
where earlier reductions may already have fixed some variables ($`lo_j = hi_j`$). Write the presolve step for one row.
Write `reduce_row(coefs, rhs, lo, hi)` in `reduce.py`. `coefs` maps each variable to $`a_j`$ (any sign, never 0), and `lo` and `hi` map it to its bounds, 0 or 1. With

\underline{L} = \sum_{a_j > 0} a_j\, lo_j + \sum_{a_j < 0} a_j\, hi_j, \qquad
\overline{L} = \sum_{a_j > 0} a_j\, hi_j + \sum_{a_j < 0} a_j\, lo_j

items: otherwise `("keep", fixings)`, where `fixings` maps each variable with $`lo_j < hi_j`$ that the row forces to a value: $`x_j = 0`$ if $`a_j > 0`$ and $`\underline{L} + a_j > b`$, and $`x_j = 1`$ if $`a_j < 0`$ and $`\underline{L} - a_j > b`$. Compute $`\underline{L}`$ once, from the bounds as given.

blocks.text: Compare as the lesson's presolve code does, with the tolerance $`\varepsilon = 10^{-9}`$ always in favour of keeping a row and leaving a variable free. Written out, the reference solution's tests are:

So a row whose most activity is $`0.1 + 0.2`$ against $`b = 0.3`$ is kept: in floating point that sum is a hair above 0.3, and deleting a row on a rounding error is the mistake the tolerance guards against.

cases.says: a row whose most activity is within the right-hand side is redundant and fixes nothing
a free 0-1 variable whose coefficient alone overruns the row is fixed at 0
a variable already fixed at 1 counts in the least activity, so it can force others to 0
when even the least activity overruns the right-hand side, the verdict is infeasible
a variable with a negative coefficient is fixed at 1 when 0 would overrun the row
a row whose most activity is above the right-hand side only by rounding is kept, not deleted
